title: Extraction of PCB18 and Its Hydroxylated Metabolites from Animal Tissues
author: Xueshu Li
materials: Cap tube-A and the Reference standard.
Invert tube-B for 5 minutes, then centrifuge.
Cap all vials immediately with a crimp cap.

Dispose of the following materials as indicated: Scalpel – sharps container. Homogenizer probe – dispose as PCB-contaminated hazardous waste. SPE cartridges – Remove the cartridges from the SPE manifold and dispose the content as PCB-contaminated hazardous waste. Place the cartridges in the sink to be washed. Evaporator – Place needles in a glass beaker and combust in the furnace. Tube-A, Tube-B, Tube-C, Tube-D, and other aqueous solutions – dispose as aqueous hazardous waste. Organic solvents (waste tubes with hexanes and 2-propanol) – dispose as organic hazardous waste. All PCB-exposed disposable glassware, foil, GC vials, and gloves – dispose as PCB-contaminated hazardous waste. Serological pipettes – sharps container.
Let the silica gel precipitate to the bottom.

steps.title: Combust all glassware
steps.instruction: Combust silica gel, glass wool, all glassware (cartridges, short and long pipettes, tubes, beaker/volumetric flask, funnel), scalpel, forceps, and spatula before use.

steps.title: Label sample tubes
steps.instruction: Label all sample tubes as Tube‑A1, A2, …; Tube‑B1, B2, …; Tube‑C1, C2, …; Tube‑D1, D2, …; and a Reference tube.

steps.title: Thaw standards
steps.instruction: Remove the Ongoing Recovery and Precision (ORP) standard (PCB18 and 4′‑OH‑PCB18) and the Surrogate Standard solutions (SS_PCB d‑PCB30; SS_OH‑PCB 4‑OH‑PCB52) from the freezer and allow them to warm to room temperature for about 30 min.

steps.title: Weigh tissue
steps.instruction: Place the tissue (e.g., liver ~100 mg or brain ~100 mg) into a Tube‑A, record the weight, and wash the scalpel, forceps and spatula between samples with water, acetone and hexanes.

steps.title: Add 2‑propanol
steps.instruction: Add 3 mL of 2‑propanol to each Tube‑A with a repeater pipettor.

steps.title: Homogenize sample
steps.instruction: Homogenize each sample for 30–60 s with a TissueRuptor; rinse the blade between samples with water followed by ~5 mL 2‑propanol.

steps.title: Add diethyl ether
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL diethyl ether to each Tube‑A in a fume hood, recap, and vortex gently.

steps.title: Add surrogate standards
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of d‑PCB30 (100 ng/mL) and 100 µL of 4‑OH‑PCB52 (100 ng/mL) to all Tube‑A samples (method blanks, tissue blanks, tissues, OPR, and Reference). This provides 10 ng of each surrogate per tube.

steps.title: Spike OPR and reference
steps.instruction: To Tube‑A OPR samples and the Reference tube only, add 100 µL PCB18 standard (100 ng/mL) and 100 µL 4′‑OH‑PCB18 standard mixture (100 ng/mL each), delivering 10 ng of each analyte.

steps.title: Set centrifuge/rotator
steps.instruction: Set centrifuge for 5 min at 3000 rpm (≈1811 g). Set tube rotator for 5 min at 40 rpm. For nitrogen evaporation steps a 35 °C water bath may be used if needed.

steps.title: Invert tube‑A
steps.instruction: Invert Tube‑A on the rotator for 5 min at 40 rpm.

steps.title: Add phosphoric acid
steps.instruction: Add 5 mL phosphoric acid (H₃PO₄) in NaCl to a new Tube‑B with a repeater pipettor.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant A→B
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant from Tube‑A to Tube‑B using a long pipette.

steps.title: Centrifuge tube‑A
steps.instruction: Centrifuge Tube‑A for 5 min at 3000 rpm.

steps.title: Second extraction solvent
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL 2‑propanol and 3 mL hexanes‑diethyl ether (9:1, v/v) to Tube‑A, vortex 10 s, then centrifuge 5 min at 3000 rpm.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant A→B again
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant from Tube‑A to Tube‑B a second time.

steps.title: Collect organic layer
steps.instruction: Transfer the top organic layer from Tube‑B to a new Tube‑C with a long pipette.

steps.title: Re‑extract tube‑B
steps.instruction: Re‑extract Tube‑B with 3 mL hexanes‑diethyl ether (9:1, v/v), vortex, and centrifuge 5 min at 3000 rpm.

steps.title: Combine extracts in C
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant from Tube‑B to Tube‑C, combining with the previous extract (≈7 mL total).

steps.title: Evaporate to 100 µL
steps.instruction: Evaporate the solvent in Tube‑C under a gentle stream of nitrogen to approximately 100 µL.

steps.title: Add methanol
steps.instruction: Add 5 drops of methanol to Tube‑C (excluding the Reference tube), vortex 5 s, and place the tubes in the fume hood.

steps.title: Derivatize with diazomethane
steps.instruction: In the fume hood, add ~0.5 mL diazomethane (using a 10 mL serological pipette) to each sample and 1 mL to the Reference tube.

steps.title: Label GC vials
steps.instruction: Label GC vials with the corresponding sample numbers.

steps.title: Thaw internal standards
steps.instruction: Remove the internal standards (IS) from the freezer and allow them to warm to room temperature for about 30 min.

steps.title: Evaporate excess reagents
steps.instruction: Evaporate the excess ether and diazomethane in a fume hood under a gentle nitrogen flow until ~200 µL remains (no yellow color).

steps.title: Dry Reference standard
steps.instruction: Evaporate the Reference standard to near dryness (~50 µL) and set it aside for the later IS spiking step.

steps.title: Prepare SPE cartridge (dry load)
steps.instruction: Prepare each SPE cartridge as follows:

substeps.instruction: Place glass wool at the bottom of the cartridge.
Add 0.2 g silica gel and 2 g acidified silica gel.
Pass 3 mL hexanes‑DCM (1:1, v/v) through the cartridge to rinse.
Add additional glass wool and pack down with the end of a glass pipette.
Replace the cartridge top and place the clean cartridge into its port.
Pass ~3 mL hexanes‑DCM (1:1) into the bottom waste tube, keeping the solvent level above the acidified silica gel.

steps.title: Set up SPE waste collection
steps.instruction: Add uncombusted waste tubes to the bottom of the SPE manifold to collect waste eluent.

steps.title: Replace waste tubes with combusted
steps.instruction: Replace the waste tubes with freshly labeled, combusted Tube‑D and align Tube‑C in a rack to match the corresponding Tube‑D positions in the SPE manifold.

steps.title: Load extracts onto SPE
steps.instruction: Slowly load the extracts from Tube‑C into the SPE cartridge with long glass pipettes, allowing the eluate to collect in Tube‑D.

steps.title: Wash SPE cartridge
steps.instruction: Rinse Tube‑C twice (2 × 0.5 mL) with hexanes‑DCM (1:1) and load the wash solvent onto the SPE cartridge.

steps.title: Elute SPE with hexanes‑DCM
steps.instruction: Add additional hexanes‑DCM (1:1) to the SPE cartridge until the eluent in Tube‑D reaches approximately 10 mL (total added ≈9 mL). Then open the SPE valve completely to flush all residual solvent into Tube‑D, maintaining a drop‑by‑drop flow and keeping the solvent level above the acidified silica gel.

steps.title: Finish SPE and collect tube‑D
steps.instruction: Turn off the manifold vacuum and remove Tube‑D from the SPE manifold.

steps.title: Concentrate tube‑D to 200 µL
steps.instruction: Concentrate the sample in Tube‑D under a gentle stream of nitrogen to about 200 µL.

steps.title: Exchange solvent with hexanes
steps.instruction: Add 3 mL hexanes to Tube‑D and reconcentrate under nitrogen to ~50 µL to exchange the solvent.

steps.title: Add internal standard
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL internal standard (PCB204, 100 ng/mL) to Tube‑D and to the Reference standard using a single‑channel pipette.

steps.title: Vortex tube‑D
steps.instruction: Vortex Tube‑D briefly.

steps.title: Transfer to GC vials
steps.instruction: Transfer the extracts from Tube‑D and the Reference standard with a long pipette into combusted crimp‑style GC vials.

steps.title: Rinse tube‑D and final volume
steps.instruction: Rinse Tube‑D with hexanes and combine the rinse with the extract in the GC vials to give a final volume of approximately 0.6 mL.

steps.title: Prepare solvent blank
steps.instruction: Fill a GC vial with hexanes (the same hexanes used for the extractions) to serve as a solvent blank.

steps.title: Store samples before analysis
steps.instruction: Store all samples, including the solvent blank, in a solvent‑proof –20 °C freezer until instrument analysis (do not use a regular freezer because solvent vapors can damage it).

steps.title: Calculate results
steps.instruction: Use the Excel worksheet supplied with the protocol to calculate PCB18 and hydroxylated metabolite levels after GC analysis.

steps.title: Store samples after analysis
steps.instruction: Store all samples, including the solvent blank, in a solvent‑proof –20 °C freezer until the data are published (same caution about regular freezers applies).

steps.title: Clean glass cartridges and needles
steps.instruction: Wash used glass cartridges with soapy water and a brush, dry them, then combust them in the furnace. Combust used needles in the furnace as well.

steps.title: Recap and refill vials
steps.instruction: After instrument analysis, recap all GC vials to minimize solvent evaporation; if necessary, refill each vial to a final volume of ~0.6 mL.

steps.title: Prepare for derivatization
steps.instruction: Gather samples, an ice box, and serological pipettes in a fume hood.

steps.title: Handle diazomethane
steps.instruction: Take the diazomethane solution in diethyl ether from the freezer and place it in the ice box inside the fume hood.

steps.title: Store tubes post‑derivatization
steps.instruction: Cap the tubes and store them in an explosion‑proof refrigerator (not a freezer) at 4–8 °C for at least 3 h or overnight (≈16 h).

steps.title: Remove air bubbles
steps.instruction: Mix each suspension with a short glass pipette tip to eliminate air bubbles.

steps.title: Mix silica gel suspension
steps.instruction: In a small beaker, mix hexanes‑DCM (1:1) with acidified silica gel (5:1), then add this suspension to the SPE cartridge.

steps.title: Rinse SPE cartridge
steps.instruction: Add 2 mL hexanes‑DCM (1:1) with a long pipette to rinse the SPE cartridge.
